messages:
maria: CI alert on PR #9182 — microbench (kv_lookup) shows ~7% throughput drop vs main. Failing threshold in CI. Saw this in the nightly perf unit run. cc @devon @ashok :eyes:
ci-bot: perf/kv_lookup_microbench: baseline=125.4k ops/s, head=116.6k ops/s, diff=-7.0% (threshold -5.0%) — detailed logs: https://ci.internal/reports/2200123456
devon: ugh. Do we have a quick bisect? Any obvious changes in batcher/kernel selector recently?
ashok: I started a quick bisect on the CI image. Early result points to commit ab12c3d4 which touched runtime/kernel_selector.cpp around the autotune heuristics. Repro locally with docker image `redwood/ci:2200123456` using the microbench script.
ashok: bisect snippet:
```
git bisect start HEAD origin/main
git bisect run ./scripts/bench/kv_lookup_bench.sh
```
Result: bad @HEAD, good @origin/main, culprit ab12c3d4 (kernel selector: prefer_small_transfer when util<0.6)
olivia: I pulled a perf flame sample (perf record) from the bisect-built binary. Key finding: the new kernel path is causing extra buffer copies on misses — memcpy time up ~30% in kv fetch hot path. Flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/2200123456 (shortlink)
maria: can you paste the hot stack?
olivia: top stacks (condensed):
- runtime::kv::fetch -> kernel_selector::select -> dispatch::small_copy_kernel -> memcpy
- previous stack used dispatch::zero_copy_kernel -> direct_gpu_copy (no host memcpy)
ashok: that matches the change — the selector now prefers small_transfer which falls back to a host memcpy path for borderline sizes. On our common sequence lengths this pushes dozens of ops to memcpy vs zero-copy.
devon: any quick mitigations? revert the heuristic or add a size threshold tweak?
ashok: patch idea: relax prefer_small_transfer to prefer_zero_copy when sequence_length >= 128 OR kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.2. I sketched a minimal patch and ran the microbench locally — restored throughput to 124.8k ops/s (within noise).
maria: can you post the patch (or PR) and we can run CI patch job? If it fixes CI we should hold the merge until we have a proper test and a perf unit added.
ashok: pushing WIP PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/9190-wip — includes unit test for selector and perf microbench regression test entry.
sre-bot: Incident note created: PERF-2026-048. Flagged rollout of runtime v2.14.3; hold until resolution.
devon: agree hold. Also add a golden run for kv_lookup in the CI perf suite pinned to main baseline to catch this earlier.
maria: +1. Also add a comment in release notes about kernel selector risk. I'll add a quick blurb and notify product.
olivia: FYI, I also instrumented kv cache metrics — under the bad selector the effective kv cache hit latency increases slightly because eviction churn rises. Might be secondary amplification.
ashok: thanks — I'll iterate on the patch and run full CI perf. If CI passes we can merge the fix and then schedule a follow-up to refine auto-tune values.
maria: thanks all. tagging @eng-oncall for visibility. :rocket:
